lines.name: Mount Tamalpais railway, Mill Valley to the summit

operators.name: Mill Valley and Mount Tamalpais Scenic Railway
Mt. Tamalpais and Muir Woods Railway

lines.summary: Steam trains from the Northwestern Pacific's station at Mill Valley up Blithedale Canyon and around the Double Bow Knot to the summit of Mount Tamalpais, 8.19 miles; visitors could ride gravity cars back down.
lines.fate_note: Abandoned under the Railroad Commission's order of August 7, 1930 (Decision No. 22765), after a toll road reached the summit; the grade is a fire road.

sources.note: "the first train being run to the end of the line on August 27, 1896".
From 1917, no mountain trains from November to February; the local to Lee Street ran all year.
Steam trains, with some returns by gravity car.
Abandonment of all service authorized August 7, 1930, effective that day: on or about August 1930 (decision 17).

lines.notes: Opens on the Railroad Commission's August 27, 1896, the first train to the end of the line, which Poor's 1898 also gives; Poor's 1897 has August 17 and its 1902 edition August 26. From 1917 its mountain trains stopped each winter. Not drawn: the Muir Woods branch from Mesa (1906 or 1907, extended by 1915), on no sheet in the repo; the annotated 1915 Tamalpais sheet at the Mill Valley Public Library (archive.org cmlpl_000900) would show it, a map to georeference by hand.

photo.caption: The double bow-knot, where the track ran alongside itself five times, with San Francisco Bay in the distance.
photo.author: Street Railway Journal
